The arrivals lead discussed a reminder about airflow checks after a rushed handover. Incident Report: Companion Animal Travel Desk Missing Connection Review. During the evening intake, a traveler arrived at the desk with a companion pet crate that had already been moved through an earlier baggage transfer. The handoff note was brief, and the team could not confirm that the crate had been checked for steady airflow before loading. The traveler was calm but worried, and the pet, Bailey, showed mild stress from the extra handling. The senior coordinator stepped in, reviewed the transfer notes, and asked for a direct check of the crate, the latch, and the ventilation points. A safety coordinator also looked at the loading path and confirmed that the crate had been placed in a position that made the airflow check harder to complete during the rush. Staff then moved the crate to a clearer work area, verified the pet was comfortable, and gave the traveler plain guidance about the next steps. <<FACT F116>> The traveler was told what support applies in a missed connection case, and the desk kept the explanation simple so there was no confusion. <<FACT F110>> 

After the immediate handling, the team recorded the handover problem as a service miss linked to unclear communication between shifts. The senior coordinator asked for a short review with the staff involved, with focus on using a fuller transfer note and pausing long enough to verify airflow before release. The safety coordinator also reminded the team to speak up when a rushed handover leaves a gap in the animal check. The follow-up plan was to add a clearer handoff prompt for companion animal cases, reinforce the visual check for crate ventilation, and remind staff to confirm the work area before closing a transfer. Aurelia Skyways will keep using this report to support steadier companion travel and reduce avoidable stress for travelers and pets. Companion Animal Travel Desk
